note: Inherited requirements with explicitly bounded source mappings. Per-stage executed evidence is scoped by evidence_target where present; an unsupported host verifies the target rejection and reports native execution unexecuted on that host. Two source routes are represented and they do not share a stage vocabulary: task-route cases (ScopedCopyTasksV1/ScopedOwnedTasksV1 and its ScopedReadSharesV1/ScopedErrorPayloadV1 extensions) read `cfg` as the checked task IR they construct, while source.mutex.guard.v1 cases (CT26/CT27/CT29/CT30) emit directly from a checked event list and have no CFG stage, so `cfg` stays unassessed for them. Mapping is not full language conformance. Several unmapped cases have recorded reasons rather than absent evidence. CT11 asks for full permission reconstructed while local shared *aliases* survive; ScopedReadSharesV1 has no local alias form at all, and in the closest measured program the party retaining the share is an unjoined child task, so mapping it would answer a different question (card T05 section 9). CT06 needs an owned-pointer copy form the grammar does not admit. CT35/CT36/CT38/CT39 are checked at model level by FlatEpochBoundV1 (card T08) but have no source syntax, hence no parser stage and no reference execution, so they stay unmapped until epoch source syntax lands.

cases.scenario: Move an owned buffer to child; child returns it; parent joins and drops
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. Linux native allocation, pointer-preserving child return, creator join and exactly-once parent drop agree with reference execution. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent uses buffer after successful move capture
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. The parent read after successful move rejects at Q600; CT01 supplies the accepted native control. Failed creation retains the original parent binding. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent and child share reads with complementary positive shares
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: one owned Buffer lent to two children with complementary halves of the 1024-unit read authority, both reading it while the parent also reads it, and Buffer writes on either side of the lending window because a write demands reconstructed exclusive authority. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and three fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - one object allocated and released exactly once across two live borrowers, a refused second creation returning only its own share, and a refused join returning none and reclaiming nothing. The complementary refusals are mapped as CT04 and CT05. This is not evidence about arbitrary schedules, other targets or the C memory model; ThreadSanitizer does not intercept C11 thrd_create, so data-race freedom rests on the checker's no-write-while-shared rule. The lending budget is over authority handed out, not a separation-logic fraction; disjoint slicing, write shares, more than two readers, byte accounting and nested workers stay refused.

cases.scenario: Parent writes while child retains a read share
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: the parent writes its Buffer while both children still hold their halves. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying LoanOutstanding { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, borrowers: [2, 3] }, which names the outstanding total and every borrower rather than the bare fact of a loan. An accepted Linux control moves the same write after both joins, so the refusal is keyed to the outstanding shares and not to writing at all. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Two children each request FULL for the same memory
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: two children each request the whole read authority for one allocation. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying ShareExceedsAuthority { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, requested: 1024 }; the excess request is refused as a whole and the outstanding total is unchanged. An accepted Linux control lends 511 and 513 of the same allocation, so the budget boundary is a boundary rather than a blanket refusal of two borrowers. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. Injected native creation failure restores the original buffer binding for read/drop, with no child or join obligation. cases.scenario: Second create fails after first succeeds
cases.expected: First task must still be joined
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedCopyTasksV1 explicit creation recovery: real source matches the second spawn result. Failure preserves the first task until the Err arm explicitly joins its exact native thread, then returns42. Success joins both children and returns7; initial failure has no child. A failure arm omitting the prior join rejects with Q600 ScopeBusy. Reference and native outcomes agree for all3 fixture creation scripts. This tests scalar copies and task obligations, not owned/loan capture restoration, arbitrary handlers or other native platforms.

cases.scenario: Child finishes but parent has not joined
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1: the native adapter waits for the actual worker body and completion-record write before creation returns to the parent. Parent read/drop of the moved Buffer before join reject at Q600 despite worker completion. The accepted control joins, consumes the owned Result and drops the original generation. Exact pointers and join-before-reclamation checks retain the allocation and environment while completed but unjoined. This is one owned Buffer, not loan/share restoration or a general scheduler proof.

cases.scenario: Backend join failure
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedCopyTasksV1 native fault evidence: a real i32-copy worker is created; successful control joins then frees the environment and returns 42. An injected native join failure establishes no quiescence and aborts before result publication or environment reclamation. The fault is supplied only by a test runtime adapter. Reference execution covers the successful control; native join failure has no returning reference transition. No source-owned payload/loan restoration, full runtime refinement or other-platform native conformance is claimed.

cases.scenario: Worker typed error after partial local acquisition
cases.expected: Clean locals, return loans, carry declared payload
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1 worker-local allocation: a real child acquires up to two Buffers, explicitly drops all acquired locals before raising WorkerError::Failed or a bound AllocError, and the creator joins before receiving the error. Four native/reference scenarios cover success, either allocation failure and creation failure with exact pointer/thread checks. Missing cleanup in either worker error arm rejects at Q600. The earlier sequential implicit-cleanup control remains separately executed. Loans, owned error payloads, arbitrary handlers and native refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Worker error payload contains owned result
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedErrorPayloadV1: exactly one owned Buffer rides an explicitly tagged worker error out of one child, through its completion capsule and its creator's join, and is taken out of the bound error exactly once. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and five fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - the success path releases all three objects inside the child, either worker allocation failure carries the parent's original identity back and releases every local it does not carry, a refused creation transfers nothing, and a refused join reclaims neither payload nor environment. Two negative controls pin that an undelivered payload and an unreleased taken payload are refused at Q600. One payload, one flat own<Buffer>: recursive owned graphs, several payloads, mixed declared rows, nested workers and loans inside payloads stay refused, and no race detector covers this backend.

cases.scenario: Worker error payload contains scoped capture borrow
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedErrorPayloadV1: a scoped capture borrow cannot leave its child inside an error payload. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q500] carrying 'an error payload requires own<Buffer>', at the raise that writes it rather than at the join. An accepted Linux control is the same program whose worker owns its payload, so the refusal is keyed to the borrowed capture and not to the raise form. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Parent `?` bypasses a live sibling task
cases.semantic_profile: Actual scoped-copy task source checking: a second spawn with immediate ? has a dynamic failure edge leaving the first live handle, and rejects with Q600 ScopeBusy. The separate joined_sibling.qcore control joins the first task before creating the second; Linux checking/reference execution accepts it with both children joined. The rejected case executes parser/type checker only. No resource capture, sibling recovery handler or native execution of the rejected program is claimed.

cases.scenario: In-scope handler joins siblings before rethrow
cases.expected: Accept with all result obligations accounted
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1: an in-scope second-creation error handler joins the first child, drops its returned Buffer and rethrows the bound payload-free SpawnError. Four native/reference scenarios cover success, allocation failure and each creation failure with exact buffer/environment identities and join-before-reclamation checks. Omitting the sibling join or returned-buffer drop rejects at Q600. Owned error payloads, loans, arbitrary handlers, worker allocation and native refinement proofs remain open.

Two critical sections use the same mutex for the same payload
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 lowered onto the unedited CheckedMutexInvariantV1 checker: two lexical critical sections over one mutex generation and one declared footprint, on one Linux thread. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, check, independent certificate recheck, C11 emission, and a run of the emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan whose stdout agrees line for line with interpret_mutex_program over the checked event list. `cfg` is unassessed because this route has no CFG stage at all. One thread, one target, one compiler invocation: not evidence about contention, scheduling, publication or the C memory model. DeclaredFootprintShape and InvariantPredicateDeclared are carried premises, and source-to-trace refinement is unproved in both Rust and Lean.

cases.scenario: Two different mutex identities allegedly guard the same payload
cases.expected: Reject without a valid composite protocol
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a second `mutex guards` over an already protected footprint is refused at Q617 FootprintAlreadyProtected, so no composite protocol is admitted; the exact ordered cascade [Q617, Q600 UnknownMutex] is pinned. The disjoint_payloads control declares two generations over two disjoint payloads and is accepted, so the refusal is keyed to the shared payload rather than to the number of mutexes. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control compiles through the Linux-only emission path, which is what evidence_target records. No composite or nested protection protocol, lock ordering, or post-creation protection growth is established.

cases.scenario: Guard is moved to a child or unlocked by another thread
Typed error leaves a temporarily broken mutex invariant
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a typed-error exit taken with the invariant open is refused at Q614 InvariantOpenAtErrorExit, with the exact ordered cascade [Q614, Q619, Q600, Q600, Q600] pinned so the refusal is shown not to have released the guard. The restored.qcore control closes the invariant before raising the same error and is accepted, which is the scenario's `unless restored` half. Q613 and Q614 stay distinct codes: the error path is attributed separately from the normal path, and the Lean theorem typed_error_exit_obeys_the_normal_release_rule proves both exits obey the same release rule. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control is Linux-gated. The invariant predicate has no runtime representation and stays the InvariantPredicateDeclared premise.

cases.scenario: Guard-derived borrow escapes critical section
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1: a guard-derived borrow still live at its critical section's end is refused at Q615 GuardBorrowEscape, with the exact ordered cascade [Q615, Q619, Q600, Q600, Q600] pinned. Two escape mechanisms execute: this one, and the escaped_borrow control, where naming the borrow binder after its block fails at Q013 unknown name because the binder is body-local; Q013 is recorded as name resolution and deliberately not relabelled as a concurrency verdict. The released.qcore control takes the same borrow, reads through the guard and drops it inside the section, and is accepted. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; the accepted control is Linux-gated. This profile refuses task creation outright, so a borrow cannot travel to a child here at all: no claim is made that a guard is unmovable in a future profile that admits tasks.

cases.expected: Old capability cannot authorize new identity
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1 Buffer lifetime identity: two successful root allocations are separated by real munmap/mmap at the same numeric address using MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE.
